sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Carteret, then recently renamed from Roosevelt, at 50 feet to an inch. The main axis is Roosevelt Avenue, lettered also as Rahway Avenue, which crosses the sheet from left to right and is lined on both sides with continuous rows of stores, many of brick and drawn in pink, with dwellings and a few other uses behind them. A fire department with hook and ladder company stands on the south side near the middle. Running up the sheet from Roosevelt Avenue are John Street (also lettered St. John), Lefferts Street and Lafayette Street, with Railroad Avenue and the line of the Sound Shore Division of the New Jersey railroad running diagonally through the centre; a passenger station, waiting room and freight house sit just south of Roosevelt Avenue beside the tracks. North of Roosevelt Avenue the blocks hold small frame dwellings on narrow lots, with George Chamra and Sons, coal and ice, with coal bins, near Forsyth Place. South of the avenue are a hall, a garage, a laundry service company, the Carteret Inn restaurant, a plumbing shop and a lumber and planing mill with a contractor's yard along Sharot Street at the foot of the sheet. Fitch Street crosses the lower part and Pershing Avenue, also lettered Colwell, runs up the left edge. The adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 7 on the left, 3 on the right, 5 below and 8 above. A scale bar and the map division stamp of Princeton University Library appear near the bottom.
notes: Roosevelt Avenue keeps its name today; Rahway Avenue is the alternative name lettered beside it.
Fitch is Fitch Street today; Pershing Avenue, Lafayette Street, Lefferts Street, John Street and Sharot Street keep their names.
The town was named Roosevelt until 1922; the sheet is lettered Carteret.
Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (fitted 7.96 px per foot), unlike the 100 foot sheets of most of the volume.
Scale 50 ft to an inch. Roosevelt Avenue (also lettered Rahway Av.) business centre with John, Lefferts, Lafayette, Fitch, Sharot and Pershing. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the Warner Chemical Company works on the Staten Island Sound shore at the eastern end of Carteret, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Roosevelt Avenue runs down the sheet from Lafayette Street at the top, then turns west as Roosevelt Avenue, also lettered Woodbridge Avenue, near the middle of the lower half. Tompkins Avenue crosses the works from the Roosevelt Avenue side towards the east. A line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, lettered as the New Jersey Terminal Railroad, crosses the upper part from side to side, with a freight house of the Central Railroad of New Jersey and sidings at the upper right. Most of the sheet is occupied by the Warner Chemical Company chemical works, drawn as large pink and yellow manufacturing buildings, with an office building and chemical storage buildings, a machine shop, a rock storage building, an acid house, tanks and many smaller works buildings, with watchman and fire-fighting notes at the right. West of Roosevelt Avenue the ground is largely open, with a few dwellings along the upper left and a stretch of undivided land numbered as blocks. A ferry slip, piers and storage structures project into Staten Island Sound along the bottom edge, where the shoreline is drawn in blue. The compass is in the lower left, the scale bar and map division stamp of Princeton University Library at the bottom, and the neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins.
notes: Placed from a single hand-picked junction (Lafayette Street and Roosevelt Avenue) with the scale taken from sheet 2 and rotation from the compass; low confidence.
The works and most of the streets drawn here have been rebuilt; only Roosevelt Avenue and Lafayette Street survive as modern streets.

Scale 50 ft to an inch, drawn turned about 90 degrees from sheet 2 (Roosevelt Av. runs up the page). Warner Chemical Co. works, Tompkins Av., C.R.R. of N.J. and N.J. Terminal R.R., Staten Island Sound shore. Anchored on one hand-picked point (Lafayette / Roosevelt); low confidence.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows a residential and light commercial part of Carteret south and south-west of the town centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Wheeler Avenue, also lettered Roosevelt Avenue, runs across the top; below it, long narrow blocks between Leick, Randolph, Sharot and Fitch Streets carry rows of small frame dwellings, a church, a public school and a few stores, with Roosevelt Avenue, also lettered Railway Avenue, forming the right margin. The left third of the sheet is cut by Noe Creek, drawn in blue and winding from the upper left to the foot of the sheet, with Whittier, Longfellow, Lowel, Emerson and Blanchard Streets laid out on the west bank and Pershing Avenue crossing the creek. The centre of the sheet, between Noe Street and Harris Street, is platted in narrow lots but almost entirely unbuilt. Below Pershing Avenue the sheet is largely open land numbered in blocks, crossed by two railroad lines running diagonally from the lower left to the right, one lettered Central Railroad of New Jersey, with a coal and lumber yard near Randolph Street. Houses cluster again near Lafayette Street at the foot of the sheet. The compass is at the upper left, the scale bar and the map division stamp of Princeton University Library at the bottom right; adjoining sheets 6, 7, 2, 4, 13 and 17 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Hazel Street is not in the modern street data; Wheeler Avenue, Sharot Street, Leick Avenue, Randolph Street, Harris Street, Noe Street, Fitch Street, Blanchard Street and Pershing Avenue appear today under the same names.
Lowel is lettered without a suffix; modern Lowell Street.
Names read at overview resolution; a few street labels near the creek were not legible and are left out.
Scale 100 ft. Noe Creek residential district: Wheeler Av. (printed also as Roosevelt Av.), Leick, Randolph, Sharot, Pershing. Turned about 67 degrees.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows a fan-shaped residential district in the west of Carteret, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with its streets running at an angle to the page. Four long streets, Catherine, Randolph, Mary and Tennyson, cross the sheet from the north-east to the south-west, cut by Steiner Street and Washington Avenue, which runs diagonally across the middle, and by Edgar, Heald and Thornall Streets lower down. The upper right is laid out with Lexington, Whitman and Holmes Avenues and blocks numbered in the 300s; Duffy Street forms the upper left edge. Nearly all blocks are subdivided into narrow lots and carry small frame dwellings, with a few stores along Washington Avenue and near Wheeler Avenue at the foot of the sheet, where Randolph and Sharot Streets meet the street lettered Wheeler, also lettered Roosevelt Avenue. Roosevelt Avenue, also lettered Rahway Avenue, runs along the right margin. Much of the central and upper right area is only partly built up, and the right-hand blocks are almost empty. The compass is at the left, the scale bar and the map division stamp of Princeton University Library at the bottom right, and sheet numbers 10, 11, 16, 7, 5 and 13 are given at the margins.
notes: Fitted at about 3.69 px per foot against about 3.96 on neighbouring sheets, with residuals of 6 to 12 m at most junctions: the drawn blocks are narrower than the modern street spacing, so the placement is low confidence.
Some street lettering at the left edge and in the upper right was not legible at overview resolution and is left out.

Scale 100 ft. Fan-shaped residential district (Duffy, Catherine, Randolph, Mary, Tennyson, Washington Av.). Fits poorly: residuals 2 to 12 m on nearly every junction, scale 7 percent under sheets 5 and 7; low confidence.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows a regular grid of residential blocks in Carteret, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, between Roosevelt Avenue on the west, also lettered Rahway Avenue, and open land to the east. The cross streets are Hayward Avenue, Christopher, Charles and John (also lettered St. John), and the avenues running up the sheet are Lincoln Avenue (also lettered Thomas), Grant Avenue (also lettered Robert), Jeannette, St. Ann and Beverly. Blocks are numbered in the 60s, 70s, 100s and 200s and are divided into narrow lots, most carrying small frame dwellings, with stores concentrated along Roosevelt Avenue, an institutional building and a theatre or hall in the left blocks, and a brass or metal works near St. Ann Street. In the upper left a separate group of wedge-shaped blocks lies along Gantz Avenue and Roosevelt Avenue, drawn with lots at a different angle. East of Beverly Street the sheet is open land, crossed by a diagonal private road, and at the top the Mexican Petroleum Corporation tank farm is shown with oil tanks and a gauger's building. The compass is at the upper left, the scale bar and the map division stamp of Princeton University Library at the bottom right; adjoining sheets 16, 6, 5, 2 and 8 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Lincoln Avenue, Grant Avenue, Jeannette Street, Beverly Street, Hayward Avenue, Christopher Street, Charles Street and John Street keep their names today; Gantz Avenue and St. Ann are not in the modern street data.
Thomas and Robert appear in parentheses beside Lincoln and Grant.
Scale 100 ft. Residential grid on Roosevelt Av., Lincoln, Grant, Jeannette, Beverly, Pershing.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows a lightly built-up residential edge of Carteret, then lately renamed from Roosevelt, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run square to the page. In the upper left, John Street runs across the sheet with a row of frame dwellings along its south side, crossed by Jeannette Street at the left and Beverly Street at the right; Florence and Hillside Place run down the left side. Lefferts Street, 50 feet wide, runs across the blocks below, which are platted into narrow lots with block numbers 393, 397 and 205. Lafayette Street crosses the lower part, with a coal and ice yard and a few buildings near the left edge. A tangle of Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks, including the Sound Shore line and a Reformatory track, crosses the middle of the sheet diagonally and runs south to the works of the American Agricultural Chemical Company and Williams and Clark Fertilizer Works at the Staten Island Sound shore, with their large storage and manufacturing buildings, a pier and a bank of tanks at the lower right. A private road is lettered across the top right. The compass is at the upper left and the scale note at the upper right.
notes: Jeannette, John, Beverly, Lefferts and Lafayette survive in OpenStreetMap; Florence and Hillside Place do not.
Sheet is turned about 72 degrees from the other sheets' grid; fitted rotation is from three junctions.
Street names are as printed, some without a street suffix; Jeannette read from a cropped label.
Scale 100 ft, turned about 72 degrees. John, Jeannette, Beverly, Lefferts, Lafayette; rail lines and a works at the Sound. Three points; medium confidence.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers a largely undeveloped residential subdivision in the western part of Carteret (then lately renamed from Roosevelt), drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The part is laid out as a regular grid of avenues named for presidents, Jackson, Van Buren, Harrison, Tyler, Polk, Taylor and Fillmore Avenues, running across the sheet between Chestnut Street on the west and Oak Street on the east, with East Elm and East Cherry Streets crossing them. Carteret Avenue cuts diagonally through the western blocks from Jackson Avenue towards Fillmore Avenue, leaving several wedge-shaped blocks subdivided into narrow lots. The N. J. Terminal Railroad runs along the western side of the sheet, beside Chestnut Street. Nearly every block is platted into narrow building lots with lot numbers along the frontages, but only a scattering of buildings is drawn, almost all small one- and two-storey frame dwellings with a few outbuildings; the blocks east of Cherry Street and south of Taylor Avenue are almost empty. Below Fillmore Avenue the sheet is open, unplatted land with block numbers only. In the lower right corner a strip of lots on Duffy Street, with the end of Mary Street, belongs to the area of Sheet 6 and is marked with that sheet's key number. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered at the block ends. A Princeton University Library map division stamp lies in the open ground near the bottom of the sheet.
notes: East Elm and East Cherry are today Elm Street and Cherry Street; Van Buren Avenue is Vanburen Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Duffy Street and Mary Street in the lower right corner continue on Sheet 6.

Pilot. Scale 100 ft to an inch. Jackson to Fillmore Avenues between Chestnut and Oak Streets (Elm and Cherry printed as E. Elm and E. Cherry); N.J. Terminal R.R. along the west side; Duffy and Mary Streets in the bottom right corner. One part, mask null.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows a sparsely built part of western Carteret, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, whose streets run at a steep angle to the page. Carteret Avenue crosses the left of the sheet from top to bottom, and Washington Avenue runs up the sheet from the foot and then bends north-east to the right edge, crossing Cypress Street and Linden Street, which run to the left towards Carteret Avenue. A single block of narrow lots on Louis Street, east of Washington Avenue, carries the only cluster of buildings, small frame dwellings with a few outbuildings; the rest of the sheet is open land numbered in blocks, with Whittier Street at the foot. A strip along the right margin belongs to the adjoining sheet 6 and shows the ends of Duffy, Randolph, Steiner, Catherine, Edgar, Heald and Thornall Streets, with a few houses on Edgar and Heald Streets. The compass is in the upper left, the scale bar and the map division stamp of Princeton University Library at the bottom left, and the neighbouring sheets 10, 6, 12 and 13 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Placed from four junctions almost along one street (Washington Avenue) with a helmert transformation; low confidence.
Carteret Avenue junctions were not detected.
Scale 100 ft. Sparse blocks on Carteret Av., Washington Av., Louis, Cypress, Linden; four points nearly in a line, helmert; low confidence.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the central residential part of Carteret, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and printed upright on the scan. It is divided by the line of the N. J. Terminal Railroad and Terminal Avenue, which run from top to bottom near the middle of the sheet. East of that line is a regular grid of blocks cut by Linden, Whittier, Longfellow, Lowell, Emerson, Pershing Avenue, Atlantic and High Streets, running across the sheet between Terminal Avenue and Carteret Avenue on the right edge, with Central Avenue as the main north-south street between them. Alternative names are lettered in parentheses beside several streets, for example Arch beside Longfellow, Orange beside Lowell and Bryant beside Pershing Avenue. The blocks are laid out in narrow lots and are built up with small frame dwellings in the middle and lower rows, with a hall, a Polish Catholic church, the American Club and the Cleveland public school among the larger buildings, and a school at the lower right. West of the railroad the grid turns about 45 degrees: Grant, Laurel, Ash, Birch, Spruce, Holly and Larch Streets and Arthur and McKinley Avenues are platted as long narrow lots, mostly unbuilt except for a cluster of dwellings and shops near Roosevelt Avenue and Pershing Avenue at the lower left. A compass rose and the Princeton map division stamp lie in the open ground at the bottom left. Block numbers run from 85 to 259.
notes: Roosevelt Avenue (Woodbridge Avenue) is today Roosevelt Avenue; Arthur Avenue, Holly, Larch, Spruce, Birch, Laurel and Ash are Street or Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Sheet number and the stamp reading are from the 1600 px overview and the three full-resolution crops of the part; printed alternative names in parentheses are listed as separate entries.
Scale 100 ft. Dense residential grid in two directions (Grant, Laurel, Ash, Arthur Av., Roosevelt Av., Pershing). One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 shows the central grid of Carteret, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and scanned upside down, so north is toward the bottom of the image. It continues Sheet 12 to the east and shows the blocks on both sides of Washington Avenue, which runs from top to bottom through the middle of the sheet. Streets running across the sheet are, from the bottom, Linden, Whittier, Longfellow (Arch), Lowell (Orange), Emerson, Pershing Avenue (Bryant), Atlantic, High, Locust and Roosevelt Avenue at the top, with Carteret Avenue on the right edge and Blanchard and Shaffer Streets on the left side. The blocks east of Washington Avenue are mostly platted into narrow lots with a scattering of dwellings; to the west the lots are larger with a denser frame housing along Pershing Avenue, Cooke Avenue and Emerson Street, and a few brick or tile buildings. A creek enters at the left edge near the top of the picture, and the compass rose is at the lower left. Block numbers on the sheet run from 88 to 238.
notes: A street lettered near Emerson on the left of the sheet could not be read confidently and is left out.
Printed alternative names (Bryant, Orange, Arch) are today Pershing Avenue, Lowell Street and Longfellow Street.
Scale 100 ft, scanned upside down. Residential grid on Roosevelt Av., Washington Av., Pershing, Emerson, Lowell, Longfellow, Locust.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows part of the Pershing Avenue and Salem district of Carteret, scanned upside down so that north is toward the bottom. Unlike the 100 foot sheets around it, the part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Warren, Union and Essex Streets run across the sheet, lettered with their older designations (C Street, B Street and A Street), crossing Pershing Avenue (Delamar Avenue) in the middle and Salem (E Street) on the right. Hudson (Houston) Street runs along the left side with Burlington (Thomas) Street beside it, and Roosevelt Avenue (Woodbridge Avenue) crosses the lower third of the sheet, with Larch Street and McKinley Avenue below it and Terminal Avenue at the lower left. The upper half is mostly frame dwellings on narrow lots with some vacant blocks; along Roosevelt Avenue the frontage is continuous stores and dwellings, and a large brick factory complex of the north side of Roosevelt Avenue near Pershing Avenue is shown in pink. The edge of Woodbridge Township is lettered along the right margin. The Princeton map division stamp lies at the top and the compass rose at the lower right.
notes: Warren, Union and Essex Streets are printed with the older names C Street, B Street and A Street in parentheses; Salem Avenue was E Street; Burlington Street is not in OpenStreetMap.
Fitted px_per_ft is about 8.15, consistent with a 50 foot sheet; the printed scale was not read on a full-resolution crop.
Scale 50 ft (by fit, 8.15 px/ft), scanned upside down. Warren, Union, Essex, Pershing, Salem, Hudson (old names in parentheses: C, B, A, E Streets, Houston).

sheet-15-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 15 is the lower and larger part, scanned upside down so that north is toward the bottom and drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It is separated from the upper block by a heavy line that runs across the sheet and turns to the upper right. It shows the blocks between Warren Street along the bottom and Bergen Street in the upper middle, with Mercer Street between them, crossed by Hudson (Houston) Street on the left, Pershing Avenue (Delamar Avenue) in the middle and Salem Avenue on the right. The blocks are narrow frame dwellings, with a larger group of tile or brick buildings near the lower left and left centre, and some vacant lots in the upper right. Street letters in parentheses give older names, among them Seymore, D Street and C Street. The compass rose lies on the left and the part number 14 and 15 appear as neighbouring sheet numbers at the margins.
notes: Read from the 1600 px overview; some small street labels could not be read at that resolution and are left out.
Warren Street, Mercer Street and Bergen Street match OpenStreetMap names.

Scale 50 ft (by fit), scanned upside down. Two parts: part 1 the lower grid (Warren, Mercer, Bergen, Pershing, Salem, Hudson); part 2 the upper block (Chrome Av., Passaic, Somerset, Jessie, Union) beyond a heavy line, about 26 degrees from part 1; part 2 low confidence (four points).

sheet-15-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 15 is the upper block above the heavy dividing line, scanned upside down and drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It shows the edge of the Chrome Avenue district at the top, where a row of pink brick dwellings fronts Chrome Avenue, and below it blocks of narrow lots divided by Passaic and Somerset Streets running across the block, with Jessie Street on the left, Hudson (Houston) Street at the right and Union Street (Arthurkill Avenue) along the bottom edge against the heavy line. Block numbers are 162, 166, 167 and 169. A compass arrow and the neighbouring sheet numbers 14, 15, 16 and 19 are lettered on the margins. A scale and the Princeton map division stamp stand at the top right.
notes: Read from the 1600 px overview, not a full-resolution crop; street names may be incomplete.
Only four control points; rotation differs from part 1 by about 26 degrees. Low confidence.

Scale 50 ft (by fit), scanned upside down. Two parts: part 1 the lower grid (Warren, Mercer, Bergen, Pershing, Salem, Hudson); part 2 the upper block (Chrome Av., Passaic, Somerset, Jessie, Union) beyond a heavy line, about 26 degrees from part 1; part 2 low confidence (four points).

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 16 is the lower left block of the sheet, scanned upside down and drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows the platted blocks on the west side of Roosevelt Avenue (Rahway Avenue), which runs from top to bottom through the part, with Herman, Frederick, Dorothy, William and Bernard Streets crossing from Roosevelt Avenue to Park Avenue at the left edge. Nearly all the lots are narrow and vacant, with block numbers from 37 to 52; a few small dwellings stand along Roosevelt Avenue near its crossings with Herman Street and Claus Street, and open land with a few small buildings fills the strip beside the avenue. A compass rose and a map division stamp lie at the bottom and at the top. Heavy lines mark the boundary with the upper part and with the right hand part.
notes: Herman, Claus and Bernard are Hermann Street, Clauss Street and Bernard Street in OpenStreetMap.

Roosevelt Avenue junctions are from one street only, so the placement is a helmert; Park Avenue is drawn about 25 feet wide against 50 feet today and was left out. Read from the overview, not a full-resolution crop.

Scale 100 ft, scanned upside down. Three parts divided by heavy lines: part 1 lower left on Roosevelt Av. (Hermann to Bernard), helmert from points along Roosevelt Av.; part 2 top (Hudson / Union area, not placed); part 3 lower right (Grant, Lincoln, Herbert, Roosevelt), anchored on one hand-picked point. Parts 1 and 3 low confidence.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: top part beyond both heavy lines (Hudson / Union area) (no modern junction found in it; needs carried points from sheets 14, 15-2, 17 or 18).

sheet-16-3.description: Part 3 of Sheet 16 is the lower right block, scanned upside down and drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It is turned at a different angle from the rest of the sheet. It shows Grant Avenue, Lincoln Avenue (Thomas) and Roosevelt Avenue (Rahway Avenue) running as three parallel streets, with Gantz Avenue across their upper ends and Herbert Avenue and Roosevelt Avenue across the lower ends, then Columbus Avenue and Lexington Avenue in the lower right. The blocks, numbered 60, 62, 63, 64, 66 and 407, are platted in narrow lots with a few small dwellings and a hall along Lincoln Avenue and Roosevelt Avenue and a larger group of dwellings near the lower right. The upper blocks are partly vacant.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point (Herbert Avenue / Lincoln Avenue / Roosevelt Avenue) with scale and rotation from the config; low confidence.
Part of the names (Columbus and Lexington) were read from the overview only.

Scale 100 ft, scanned upside down. Three parts divided by heavy lines: part 1 lower left on Roosevelt Av. (Hermann to Bernard), helmert from points along Roosevelt Av.; part 2 top (Hudson / Union area, not placed); part 3 lower right (Grant, Lincoln, Herbert, Roosevelt), anchored on one hand-picked point. Parts 1 and 3 low confidence.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: top part beyond both heavy lines (Hudson / Union area) (no modern junction found in it; needs carried points from sheets 14, 15-2, 17 or 18).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 was scanned upside down; its lettering reads inverted. It shows the American Agricultural Chemical Company's Liebig Works, a large fertilizer manufacturing plant, on the shore of Staten Island Sound at the top of the scan, with long yellow storage buildings, a pink digester building, acid chambers and a bank of tanks, linked by railroad tracks to the Central Railroad of New Jersey and the New Jersey Terminal Railroad lines that cross the middle of the sheet. A tidal creek runs down the left side. In the lower part of the sheet Roosevelt Avenue, also lettered Woodbridge Av., runs diagonally with a row of small frame dwellings on its south side, crossed by Washington Avenue and by Liebig Lane running north to the works. Locust Street and a short street at its left lie in the lower left, below the avenue. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with the compass and scale bar at the lower left of the scan, and the key numbers 4, 5, 13 and 18 mark the neighbouring sheets.
notes: Liebig Lane is a service way in OpenStreetMap and is not used for control.
Scanned upside down: placement is rotated about 180 degrees from the upright sheets.
Scale 100 ft (assumed), scanned upside down. Works and rail lines near the Rahway River; anchored on one hand-picked point (Locust / Washington); low confidence.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the Staten Island Sound shore of Carteret at 100 feet to an inch, a largely industrial strip drawn upside down on the scan. Along the top the sound runs across the sheet, with a concrete dock and a fan of railroad sidings reaching it at the upper left. In the left centre is the lumber and veneer works of Ichabod T. Williams and Sons: a saw mill, veneer mills, lumber storage, an office and a group of veneer storage sheds, with a long shipping and storage building further south. Dotted fire-main lines and hydrants (DH) surround the works. On the right edge the Metal and Thermit Corporation chemical works occupies a strip beside the tracks, with a foundry, a washing building, a chamber building, a laboratory, sheds and storage. A broad band of tracks of the N. J. Terminal and Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the lower part of the sheet from left to right and passes a water tower at the right. Below it a short section of street grid appears at the bottom right: Middlesex Street along the tracks, and Union (Arthurkill Avenue) running south with Jessie and Passaic Streets crossing it and Somerset Street at the sheet's foot. At the bottom left Roosevelt Avenue (Woodbridge Avenue) runs diagonally to its junction with Carteret Avenue. Large parts of the interior are blank, and the left edge carries buildings continued on sheet 17.
notes: Placed from only two junctions (Union / Jessie and Union / Passaic, about 68 m apart) as a helmert: low confidence.
Union (Arthurkill Avenue) is Union Street today; Middlesex Street is now Middlesex Avenue, rebuilt with Port Carteret Drive.
Roosevelt Avenue (Woodbridge Avenue) is Roosevelt Avenue today.
Scale 100 ft, scanned upside down. Rail yard, lumber and veneer works, Metal & Thermit works, Sound shore. Helmert from Union / Jessie and Union / Passaic; low confidence.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the large steel and copper works on the Staten Island Sound shore of Carteret, at 100 feet to an inch and drawn upside down on the scan. The sound and a tidal creek run along the top, with a dock at the upper left and a long pier with hydrants jutting into the creek. The left half of the sheet is the Chrome Steel Works: an open hearth building, a bar mill, a rolling mill, a machine shop, furnace and other buildings with lettered occupancy notes, storage at the upper left and a reservoir. The centre and right belong to the United States Metals Refining Co, Copper Refinery, whose casting house, tank house, power house, laboratory, reservoirs and warehouses are drawn in pink, grey and brown, with open coal and ore bins, a blast furnace and many fire hydrants and water mains. Curving railroad sidings loop through the works and join a broad band of tracks, the N. J. Terminal R.R. and Central Railroad of New Jersey, across the bottom. Below the tracks, at the lower left, a small residential block (number 170) is laid out in narrow lots between Union (Arthurkill Avenue), Jessie Street and Chrome Avenue, with a row of dwellings along Chrome Avenue. A note on the sheet says admittance is refused and information is from a 1916 map.
notes: Placed from two junctions (Union / Jessie, shared with sheet 18, and a hand-picked Chrome Avenue / Middlesex Avenue) as a helmert: low confidence.
The parenthetical (Arthurkill Av.) is printed along the railroad edge of block 170 as well as under Union; Union Street and Middlesex Avenue are the modern names.
A water tank with 50000 gallons is drawn beside the tracks at the left.
Scale 100 ft, scanned upside down. Chrome Steel Works and U.S. Metals Refining Co. copper refinery. Helmert from Union / Jessie and a hand-picked Chrome / Middlesex point; low confidence.
